tagline: From the Conemaugh to West Virginia, by fort and falls.
intro: PA 711 leaves the Conemaugh River at Seward and runs south through Ligonier and Stahlstown, over the Turnpike at Donegal and on to Normalville. There PA 381 takes over for the run south through Mill Run and Ohiopyle to the West Virginia line, 68 miles in all.

This is the high country of Pennsylvania, Laurel Hill and Chestnut Ridge of the Alleghenies, generally cooler and wetter than most of the state. South of Mill Run the road crosses the Youghiogheny at Ohiopyle on the highway bridge and heads on through forest and farm toward Farmington.

moments.title: Fort Ligonier
moments.text: General Forbes's men built the post at Loyalhanna in 1758 on the new road to Fort Duquesne, and in its eight years as a garrison no enemy ever took it.

moments.title: Fallingwater
moments.text: Just west of the road at Kauffman, Frank Lloyd Wright designed a Pittsburgh department-store owner's weekend house partly over a waterfall on Bear Run.

moments.title: Ohiopyle
moments.text: The name comes from a Lenape phrase meaning "it turns very white", for the falls on the Youghiogheny, the same falls that made George Washington give up on the river as a road.
